transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hi there, I'm Dora. I'm a clinical conversational agent here to help you with any questions you might have about your cataract surgery recovery. Do you have any questions for me?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi Dora, yes, I do have some questions. First, I'm wondering when I can start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You can go back to light exercise, such as gardening, one week after surgery. Just be sure to avoid strenuous or heavy exercise for a month. Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Great, thanks for letting me know. Another thing I'm curious about is when I can start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: If you were using eye drops or gels before your operation, such as for dry eyes, it's safe to continue using them, unless you've been told otherwise. Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: That's good to hear. I've also noticed that I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: It's normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to the new lenses. However, if you have significant pain when it's bright, or severe light sensitivity, especially if your eye is also red and painful, we may need to assess this further. If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, we recommend wearing sunglasses when you go outside. Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thanks for the advice. One more thing — should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: It's common for your vision to not be completely clear in the first week after your operation. This should improve quickly and settle down over time. If your vision is still blurry, or getting significantly worse, we may need to check it to make sure everything is okay. Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No, that's all my questions for now. Thanks so much for your help, Dora!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're welcome! Just to confirm, have all your questions been answered?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, they've all been answered. Thanks again!

verdict.label: pass
